sentences.text: ORAL JUDGMENT

This appeal has been preferred by the appellant - Oriental Insurance Company Ltd., - org. opponent No.3 against the respondent Nos.1 and 2 - original claimants, respondent Nos.3- original opponent No.2 and respondent nos. 4, 5 and 6 - org.

NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2112/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 16/06/2023 undefined opponent nos.4, 5 and 6 under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act (for short the Act) being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgment and award passed by the learned MACT (AUX), Palanpur in MACP No.102 of 2001 on 01/01/2008.
The parties herein are referred to as they stood in the original claim petition for the sake of brevity, clarity and convenience.

2. Brief facts that emerge from the record are as under:
2.1 That on 02/12/2000 at around 10:30 pm, the claimant No.1 was taking his deceased son-Vishnubhai Chaturvedi for treatment in Ambulance bearing Registration No.RJ-24E-0485 from Abu Road to Mahesana and when they reached near RTO Office, Palanpur on the highway towards Ahmedabad near Biharibaug,
truck bearing Registration No.GRW 2550 which belonged to opponent no.2 and was insured with the opponent no.3 was parked stationary in the middle of the road without any side-signals or lights or any obstacles and

the Ambulance in which the deceased was travelling and was driven by opponent no.4 which belonged to opponent no.5 and was insured with opponent no.6 dashed at the back side of the stationary parked truck; as a result of which Vishnubhai sustained serious injuries and he was taken for treatment to Civil Hospital, Palanpur where he succumbed to his injuries.

The offence was registered at Palanpur City Police Station being I-CR No.323 of 2000.
3.

The claimants who were parents of the deceased filed the claim petition mainly stating that they had lost their son and claimed an amount of Rs.14,38,428/- under all available heads NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2112/2008 JUDGMENT DATED:
16/06/2023 undefined jointly and severally from all the opponents.
4. Notices were duly served to all the opponents and the opponent no.2 appeared but did not file any written statement

, the opponent nos.3 and 6 - insurance companies appeared and file their written statements at Exh.28 and Exh.14 respectively.
5. The opponent nos.3 and 6 - insurance companies mainly denied all the contents of the claim petition.

6. The learned tribunal after having considered the evidence on record held all the opponents jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation and held that the Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd vs Damodarprasad Kamlashankar ... on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37711063/
2 accident occurred due to 50% each negligence on the part of the driver of the ambulance and the driver of the truck and granted an amount of Rs.7,02,000/- to the claimants with 9% interest from the date of the application till the realization.

sentences.text: The learned tribunal has considered the notional income of Rs.3,500/- per month of the deceased and added 50% prospective income and deducted 1/3 rd for personal expenses and granted future loss of dependency of Rs.6,72,000/- after applying multiplier of 16 and also granted an amount of Rs.25,000/- as loss of expectancy of life and love and affection and amount of Rs.5,000/- towards funeral expenses.
7. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the said award, the appellant - org. opponent no.3 - insurance company of truck has filed the present appeal before this Court.

8. I have heard learned Advocate Mr.Nanavati appearing for the appellant and though served none has appeared for the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2112/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 16/06/2023 undefined contesting respondents.
9.
No Cross-Objection has been filed by the claimants in this matter.

11. I have gone through the R & P of the present appeal where- NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2112/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 16/06/2023 undefined from it appears that the accident had occurred on 02/12/2000 at 10:30 pm on the highway road opposite Biharibaug near RTO Office, Palanpur.

The claimant no.1 has deposed before the learned tribunal on oath at Exh.24 and the claimant no.1 who is the father of the deceased has stated that he was travelling in the ambulance and taking his son for treatment and at that time he sat in front in the Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd vs Damodarprasad Kamlashankar ... on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37711063/
3 ambulance.

sentences.text: That as they reached at the place of accident, the truck in question which was lying stationary on the road in dark was lying without any side-signals or lights or any obstacles and the ambulance in question dashed into the stationary truck from its behind.

The witness has further stated that his deceased son was 24 years old hale and hearty and had no diseases and he was working as a Reporter in Daily Newspaper "Rajasthan Patrika" and was earning Rs.4,000/- per month and he had also finished his LLB Final Examination and was also enrolled as an Advocate and working as Junior Advocate with Senior Advocate Mr.I D Acharya.

The claimants have claimed under all heads the amount of Rs.14,38,428/- and the witness has been cross-examined by the learned Advocates for both the insurance companies wherein the witness has categorically stated that the truck was lying on the road on the left side but the witness has denied that half portion of the truck was on the raw edge of the road.
Admittedly, the accident occurred at around 10:00 pm and at that time, it was dark and as they were going to hospital, the ambulance was going on in full speed.
The witness who is an eye-witness to the accident has categorically stated that there were no signal lights or any obstacles placed by the stationary truck on the road.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2112/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 16/06/2023 undefined 12.
The learned tribunal has considered all these factors and has considered the Panchnama produced at Exh.35 and from the Panchnama, it appears that there were no obstacles lying behind the truck.

The learned tribunal has also considered the final year mark-sheet of the deceased produced at Exh.37; the identity card of Bar Council of Rajasthan produced at Exh.38 and the certificate of enrollment produced at Exh.39 and the receipt of Bar Council of Rajasthan at Exh.40 and has considered the notional income of the deceased at Rs.3,500/- per month.

The learned tribunal has deducted 1/3 rd amount for personal expenses and has granted prospective income of 50% and has used the multiplier of 16 and has thereby granted the future loss of dependency of Rs.6,72,000/- and Rs.25,000/- towards the loss of expectancy of life and love and affection and amount of Rs.5,000/- towards funeral expenses and has granted the total amount of Rs.7,02,000/-
as compensation.

13. It is pertinent to note that no Cross Objections have been filed by the claimants and the only point that has been raised by the learned advocate for the appellant is regarding 50% negligence attributed to the driver of the truck.

Considering the observations made by the learned tribunal and the evidence on record, particularly regarding the evidence of the eye-witness, who is the claimant no.1 and the fact that during the cross- examination nothing to controvert his version has come on record, the learned tribunal has rightly attributed 50% negligence on the part of the driver of the truck.

It is settled proposition of law that any driver of the vehicle who intends to park his vehicle on the road ought to take proper care and NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2112/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 16/06/2023 undefined caution and to switch-on the lights and side signals of the vehicle to park and also to place the vehicle in such a manner so that the vehicles coming from behind can see the parked vehicles on the road.
Admittedly, the accident took place at 10:30 pm in the night and as per the say of the eye-witness the side-signals or light of the trucks were not on and no obstacles were placed.

The learned Advocate for the insurance companies have not examined the driver of both the vehicles involved in the accident and considering the evidence on record, the learned tribunal has rightly attributed 50% each negligence on the part of the driver of the truck and driver Oriental Insurance Co.
